title: Guiding to good
hook: whoever guides to good gets a reward like the one who does it
tomorrow: a kid asks Amira something she can't answer. now what?

segments.voice: Lines from the week: they are communities too. Service is prayer. Even one verse. Learn and teach. Gently. And yesterday, teaching by example: show, don't tell. One more, and it ties them together.
screen: `SIX LINES.` → `SHOW, DON'T TELL.` → `ONE MORE TIES THEM TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: A friend asks where to donate a winter coat. You don't have one to give, so you send her the shelter's address. She drops it off. Whose good deed is that? In Sahih Muslim, a man comes to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with exactly that kind of gap.

His riding animal is gone, and he's stuck far from home. He asks the Prophet for a mount. The Prophet says: I have none to give you. Then another man speaks up: Messenger of God, I can point him to someone who will. And the Prophet says: whoever guides to good gets a reward like the one who does it. Like the doer. Not a smaller cut for being the middleman. Not a thank-you note. A reward like it, for the one who only knew where to look. The word for reward is ajr, a wage. In the hadith's math, the one who sent the address and the one who gave the coat are both paid for the coat. Now look back at the week. Convey even one verse: pointing. Learn and teach: pointing. Gently, and by example: pointing with your whole life. Every teacher this week was a kind of signpost, and the hadith says the signpost is paid in full. One to tell a friend tonight: in this hadith, pointing someone to the good is counted like doing it.
screen: `I HAVE NONE TO GIVE YOU.` · `I CAN POINT HIM TO SOMEONE.` · `A REWARD LIKE THE DOER'S.` · `THE SIGNPOST IS PAID IN FULL.` · then, large: `THE REWARD OF THE DOER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person looking for something good: a job lead, a class, a doctor, a place to volunteer. Write them the message that points the way, a name, a link, an address, and keep it ready to send.
screen: `ONE PERSON LOOKING.` · `THE MESSAGE THAT POINTS THE WAY.`

segments.voice: Guiding to good: pointing someone toward a good deed. In the hadith, the one who points gets the doer's reward.
One to keep: the reward of the doer, even when your part was only pointing. Two weeks, carried.

howItsDone: Muslims quote this hadith when they share a good cause, a class or a charity with others, counting the referral itself as part of the good deed.
